title: F1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix: Prohibited items at Yas Marina Circuit; rules for visitors
article_text:
As UAE gets ready to host the Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, visitors from all over the world will flock to Yas Marina Circuit. The season finale will be held from December 3 to 6, and the action goes beyond the track, after-race concerts and entertainment are set to wow spectators.

With less than a week left for one of the most prestigious sports events of the year, anticipation is building. Yas Marina Circuit, where the best of the racing world will meet, has rules in place to ensure that the motorsport event goes smoothly and safely.

Security may inspect visitors and their belongings at the circuit entrances. Anyone refusing a security check or carrying prohibited items may be denied admission. In addition, while this article is based on information from the official website, it is important to note that the final decision regarding individual items rests with venue security personnel.

Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels.

- Weapons, firearms, knives and imitation weapons.

- Illegal substances and objects prohibited under UAE law.

- Balloons and other potentially disruptive items.

- Unauthorised commercial or promotional materials.

- Animals, except service animals assisting visitors with disabilities.

- Any object considered dangerous, disruptive or unsuitable by the organiser or security personnel.

Smoking is prohibited in designated non-smoking areas.

Visitors are not allowed to bring their own food and drinks into Yas Marina Circuit. Disposable beverage containers, cans, thermos flasks, picnic baskets and cooler boxes are prohibited.

- Food required for medical reasons, accompanied by a prescription or doctor's letter.

Food and drinks can be purchased in the Fanzone and Oasis areas.

Abu Dhabi Grand Prix's website states that photography must be for personal, private and non-commercial purposes. In addition, there are certain restrictions which apply if you want to take photos and videos:

Cheering till you're hoarse for your favourite F1 driver? Supporting your icons is a part of the thrill of the event, but it is important to do so responsibly. Fan accessories must not obstruct the view of other spectators. If you are bringing flags, the handles must not exceed 1 metre. In addition, accessories displaying offensive language are prohibited. Banners, signs and promotional materials may require prior approval from the organiser.

- Large backpacks, suitcases and other items that cannot fit underneath a seat.

- Camping chairs, folding chairs, stools and other portable seating equipment.

- Umbrellas, unless purchased inside the venue.

- Skateboards, rollerblades, bicycles, scooters and hoverboards.

Visitors requiring pushchairs, medical devices or essential mobility equipment must confirm access arrangements with the organiser, prior to travelling to the venue.

- Phone with your valid digital tickets in the official Abu Dhabi GP app. Screenshots of tickets, or printed tickets are not permitted.

- Keep sunscreen handy. While UAE is in its winter season, sunglasses and a hat can help protect you from the morning heat.

- A water refillable container to help you stay hydrated.

- Hearing protection: Earplugs or ear defenders, especially for children.

- Comfortable clothing: Suitable walking shoes and a light jacket for the evening.

- Medical essentials: Necessary medication and supporting medical documentation where applicable.

title: PWHL fans in Toronto more receptive to brand sponsorship than Montreal
Dinner For Five (Billion): A look at the NFL’s media rights “menu”
article_text:
Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk reported recently that the NFL has presented prospective bidders on its new five-game media rights package a “menu” of options from which to choose. If the league is to hit its typical mid-May timeline for the release of this year’s schedule, those orders probably need to be placed in the next few weeks. Sports Media Watch examines this broadcasting “menu,” with a look at who could be at the table and what their appetite might look like.

The league has announced a record nine-game international slate for the 2026 season. Six of these are set for European markets: three in London, plus one each in Madrid, Munich and Paris. These typically air in a 9:30 AM ET window, but could also be part of the 1:00 regional games.

Two additional games are set for Rio de Janeiro (featuring the Dallas Cowboys) and Mexico City (hosted by the San Francisco 49ers). Both of these games could air in primetime or in the afternoon. There will not be a game — in Rio or elsewhere — on the Friday of Week 1; that was only allowed the last two years thanks to a calendar quirk.

The one international game that does have a date is the 49ers-Rams game in Melbourne on September 10. The game will kickoff in primetime on Thursday night, which corresponds to late Friday morning in Australia. That opening Thursday is typically occupied by the NFL’s season opener, which has been pushed back to Wednesday night this year.

Since the addition of out-of-home viewing to Nielsen audience measurement in 2020, the NFL has cracked the code on getting big audiences: occasions when Americans are likely to be gathered in homes together with family and friends. Out-of-home viewing gives a boost to viewership on Sundays, but is particularly strong on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas, and the days surrounding them. It’s why the Thanksgiving afternoon games are consistently the most-watched games of any season.

With this in mind, the NFL seeks to take advantage of any available moment over the critical holiday stretch. Reports indicate the league is considering selling a new “Thanksgiving Eve” game on Wednesday night — a night that has typically produced strong results for the NBA. That will be followed by the traditional Thanksgiving Day tripleheader, with home games for Detroit and Dallas, and then a Black Friday slate that could expand to multiple games.

Christmas Eve falls on a Thursday night, so could feature a game as part of Amazon’s Thursday Night Football or another partner. Christmas Day will feature a tripleheader, after the commissioner went on the record last year to confirm there will always be three games on Christmas Day, regardless of the day of the week the holiday falls.

The NFL is forbidden by law from televising Saturday games through the first Saturday of September to the second Saturday of December as part of the 1961 Sports Broadcasting Act’s conditions to grant the league an antitrust exemption. That would leave just four regular-season Saturdays (December 19 and 26 and January 2 and 9) for the NFL, and the league will take full advantage of them. The Week 15 games clash with the first round of the College Football Playoff on ESPN and TNT, but the league has not been shy from scheduling marquee games on broadcast TV opposite the CFP.

The next two Saturdays are wide open, and there’s no reason we couldn’t see a tripleheader on both dates. Week 18 contractually belongs to ESPN/ABC, which will air a season-finale doubleheader to be set after the results of Week 17.

All of these special entrees are a part of the league’s aggressive media strategy. The NFL is seeking to force its current partners — for whom NFL inventory is an existential asset — to pay higher rights fees, while also stripping them of inventory to sell in smaller packages. All of the league’s primary partners (ESPN, NBC, FOX, CBS, Amazon) are theoretically able to consider these smaller packages, but the point is really to sell them to outside parties for a little extra cash.

YouTube was recently reported as the frontrunner to acquire a five-game package that could include any of the options above. YouTube streamed the Rio game last year on a one-year deal, and parent company Google is the exclusive distributor of the Sunday Ticket package. Netflix and FOX were also mentioned as competing for the five-game package.

Some mouths additionally need to be fed thanks to prior contractual agreements. Peacock is owed a streaming-exclusive game, which was scheduled for a December Saturday in 2023 and 2025 and featured the Rio game in 2024. NFL Network has to carry a seven-game slate, which in the past has featured a mix of Sunday-morning international games and December Saturdays. Netflix will return with another Christmas Day doubleheader, with FOX — the only partner contractually linked to Christmas when the current rights deals were announced — airing a third game.

Beyond that, is there any limit to the number of carve-outs the league could make? And is there any limit to the number of partners? Perhaps Apple TV could get a game or two for the right price. What about TikTok, in pursuit of the league’s desire to get in front of young people? There’s evidently no reason to rule out anyone willing to put up the cash for a slice of NFL inventory.

title: GOKA Signs $350,000 Three-Year Front-of-Shirt Deal With Nigeria’s Rivers United
article_text:
Rivers United have signed a three-year front-of-shirt sponsorship with sports betting and online casino operator GOKA Sports and Casino. The club values the deal at $350,000 (approximately ₦490 million) and says it is the largest shirt sponsorship in its history. The agreement makes the Port Harcourt side one of the best-funded clubs in the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) on the commercial side, early in a season in which it is again pushing for the title.

The partnership covers three seasons, starting with the current 2026/27 campaign. Rivers United administrator Barrister Chris Green and GOKA representative Jide Odi signed it. Split evenly, it would be worth approximately $116,667 (₦163.3 million) a season, although neither party has said how payments will be structured or whether any performance or promotional obligations are attached.

GOKA, whose website names GOKA N.V. as operator and lists licence references for Nigeria and Ghana, has been building its profile in Nigerian football. Earlier this month it unveiled former Super Eagles striker Obafemi Martins as brand ambassador at an event in Lagos, as part of a push to grow in Nigeria and other African markets. A weekly presence on an NPFL shirt adds match-day visibility to what the ambassador brings.

The deal comes three months after the NPFL ended a decade without a title sponsor by signing EuroMatch to a three-year, $7.5 million agreement worth $2.5 million a season. At the unveiling, NPFL chairman Gbenga Elegbeleye said 60 per cent of the proceeds would go to the 20 top-flight clubs. Shared equally, that would come to approximately $75,000 per club each season. On a straight-line basis, GOKA's annual commitment to Rivers United is worth more than that. Clubs received a first tranche of ₦15 million (approximately $11,000) each from the EuroMatch deal earlier this season.

The comparison shows how much more a shirt can earn than a league-wide distribution, provided the club has something to sell. Rivers United finished second in 2025/26 on 67 points, one behind Rangers International, and won the league in 2022. Last season they also reached the CAF Champions League group stage for the first time since 2019. This season's continental campaign ended in the preliminary round against Côte d'Ivoire's FC San Pedro, so for now GOKA's exposure is mainly domestic, on the shirt of a regular title contender. Kwara United's one-season deal with BC.Game for 2025/26, by comparison, was worth $35,000.

Rivers United are used to long-term shirt partners. Eunisell sponsored the club, and Sharks before it, for several seasons from 2015, and was often described as the NPFL's longest-standing shirt sponsor. Moving from an oil-and-gas services company to a betting operator follows the wider pattern in Nigerian football. Betting firms now supply much of the money in the domestic game, from the league's title rights to club shirts and former internationals who serve as brand faces.

How much the deal is really worth depends on the parts still undisclosed. A headline figure spread over three seasons, possibly back-loaded or tied to results, can be worth much less in the first year than the announcement suggests.

title: F1 Qatar GP: Antonelli leads Russell in opening practice
article_text:
Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli has comfortably topped first practice at Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix, holding off Mercedes team-mate George Russell as drivers grappled with the tricky Lusail circuit.

One week on from the high-speed drag race on the streets of Las Vegas, drivers and teams were facing a completely different challenge as they sampled the high downforce motorcycle track of Lusail.

In the opening stages of the first hour of practice on the smooth swoops of the Doha track, they deployed both Pirelli's medium and hard tyre compounds to get the lay of the land and gather data.

This year's world champion Antonelli led all the way through, setting an early benchmark of 1m24.057s on mediums and then gradually chipping away on subsequent run, establishing a 1m23.217s lap after 20-odd minutes to head Mercedes team-mate Russell by seven tenths.

The Mercedes pair led the cars of Red Bull, McLaren and Ferrari as they populated the leaderboard two by two, until teams started switching to the soft-tyre compound at the halfway point.

But despite deploying the softer and faster tyre compounds, Antonelli's early benchmark proved tough to topple. Russell, who was experimenting with different wing configurations, came short by half a second, while Antonelli also couldn't touch his own medium-tyre lap as the Lusail surface became littered with gravel from the many off-track excursions.

In the Red Bull Isack Hadjar set third, 0.661 in arrears, followed by a nervous looking pair of McLaren cars in the hands of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who both conceded eight tenths, and Las Vegas winner Max Verstappen.

Ferrari was the fourth-fastest team after a muted session, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton over 1.2s adrift from Antonelli after grappling with massive front tyre degradation.

Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad led the midfield aboard the VCARB 03, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly rounding out the top 10.

title: Tickford Racing strikes significant sponsorship extension
article_text:
Castrol considered its relationship with Tickford among its most successful with 92 race wins and is the second in its motorsport sponsorship portfolio alongside M-Sport.

Castrol first partnered with the Supercars heavyweights in 2003 under the Ford Performance Racing banner, through the Prodrive period and into the Tickford era.

‍”We’re thrilled to announce the extension of the Castrol-Tickford partnership into Year 25 and beyond,” said Castrol Australia and New Zealand head of marketing Jotika Prasad.

“Castrol’s commitment to Australian motorsport is a vital part of our DNA, and Castrol’s partnership with Tickford is certainly a key element of that.

“Castrol’s global association with Ford and Ford Racing programs is something we’re very proud of, and it’s certainly special that one of our longest-standing motorsport associations is right here in Australia.”

Tickford Racing will go into 2027 with an unchanged driver line-up of Cameron Waters and Thomas Randle.

Since graduating from the Super2 Series to Supercars, Randle has carried Castrol’s colours on his cars.

“It’s fantastic to announce that Castrol has re-signed with Tickford Racing for 2027 and beyond,” Randle said.

“I’m super pumped to continue our amazing partnership, a deal that has been going for 25 years.

“It just shows incredible loyalty between Tickford Racing and Castrol and I know that it’s a partnership that is valued.

“Castrol has been my number one supporter for many years now – not only in Supercars but also through my junior ranks.

“We’ve done some amazing things together, whether at the track or off it, I just can’t wait to see what’s in store for 2027 and beyond.”

Tickford Racing chief executive officer Simon Brookhouse hailed the long-standing relationship between his team and Castrol.

‍”We are incredibly proud to continue our longstanding partnership with Castrol,” said Brookhouse.‍

“The Castrol brand is integral to who we are as a race team and without their loyal support we would not be in the position we are in today.

“Castrol’s support and passion for what we do is amazing and it allows us to continue to push boundaries within the race team.

“It goes without saying, but to be one of Castrol’s longest standing partnerships globally is something we do not take for granted and we are excited to continue with them into the future.”

title: Formula 1 News: Vasseur goes silent amid Ferrari crisis
The Inside Story on the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team’s Triumphant Season
article_text:
Last week, motorsport’s controlled maelstrom that is Formula 1 descended on Las Vegas for the 21st grand prix of the 2026 season. Yet the biggest questions, namely, who would secure the Constructors’ crown and the Drivers’ Championship title had already been answered by the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 team and its young phenom Kimi Antonelli, respectively.

Prior to Friday’s qualifying session, Bradley Lord, deputy team principal for the Mercedes squad, visited our House of Robb Las Vegas Grand Prix pop-up, located at the Allē Lounge on the 66th Floor of Resorts World. There, the second-in-command under Toto Wolff discussed why success came so decisively this season and shared insights on the team’s drivers, the tactical approach for the remainder of the season, and how the world’s premier race series has become a thriving business.

“It’s completely transformed in the last decade, from a niche sport of enthusiasts racing around the world to, you know, one of the biggest and fastest growing sports in the world, with a vastly different footprint, vastly different profile, and with that, the revenue that we’re able to generate as a team has expanded enormously,” Lord told the audience. “This year, we should hit $1 billion in revenue for the very first time, which is quite amazing for a small manufacturing company in the middle of the U.K.,” he mentioned regarding the team’s financial renaissance.

More impressive than the recent fiscal performance of Mercedes, though, has been its dominance in Formula 1 since 2014, when it began a winning streak of Constructors’ Championship titles that continued through 2021. Not only was that a legacy-defining span for the team, but also for its star driver Lewis Hamilton, who finished first in the Drivers’ Championship six of those seasons, bringing his total—so far—to seven.

The past four years have been decidedly more challenging for the Silver Arrows, especially with the series swapping to ground-effect cars, leaving Red Bull Racing and McLaren taking turns at the top. In 2025, Mercedes won only two races, while George Russell and Kimi Antonelli ended the season in fourth and seventh, respectively. This season, Antonelli had earned enough points by the end of the Mexico City Grand Prix to be crowned the overall victor, and Mercedes—winning 12 races—was the undisputed Constructors’ Champion after the contest in Brazil on November 8. So, what changed?

“Periodically in Formula 1, every sort of four five years, we have a major rules change . . . usually designed to slow the cars down, because every year they get faster, and at some point they get unsafe for the circuits we race on,” explained Lord. “And for 2026, we changed both the power units, so changed the engines—still 1.6-liter V-6 turbos, but with much more electrical energy as part of the overall power, so we’ve got over 1000 hp. Roughly 50 percent of that comes from an electric motor, 50 percent of it from the combustion engine; and around that new power unit, we put new aerodynamic regulations.” According to Lord, adapting to the new protocols also necessitated that the chassis, electronic control unit, and tires were all new as well.

The herculean course change for the cars also required reimagining what would feed the internal-combustion engines in order to complement the environmental ethos of hybridization. “Developing an advanced sustainable fuel means also developing all the infrastructure to produce that fuel as well. So that’s been an enormous job,” said Lord. “So we did the opposite of what you were always taught in chemistry or in physics at school, which is, if you do an experiment, change one thing at a time. We ripped up everything at the same time and landed with a new formula for 2026.” Of the shift in parameters dictated by Formula 1, Lord summed up the obvious by noting; “We have done a better job than the other teams in navigating that rule set.”

The transformation of Kimi Antonelli, who landed on the team’s radar when he was only around 11 years old (such was his karting prowess), has been more compelling to witness. Selected to fill the seat Hamilton vacated to join Ferrari, Antonelli had a rookie year that more than hinted at his potential, but few could have anticipated what would follow.

“It seems crazy to think that Kimi only won his first race, and got his first pole position, in China this year at the second race of the season,” said Lord. “From there, he went on a run of wins . . . five in a row that set himself up for an unexpected but quite remarkable championship challenge—he’s done all that at the age of 20, and so he’s become the first Italian champion in 73 years.” Equally noteworthy for Lord is how the young driver has handled it all. “He’s managed to both deliver something very, very exceptional, but also keep his feet on the ground and stay incredibly humble, grounded, and in touch with reality at the same time.”

His teammate George Russell’s experience, despite winning the Australian Grand Prix in March to start it all off, has been markedly different. “George has had both the strongest and the most disappointing season of his career,” mentioned Lord. “He’s had the lion’s share of the technical problems we’ve had. We’ve had a lot of unreliability in this first season with the new cars and the new engines, and he has struggled with that more than Kimi . . . he’s had a season that’s really tested his resilience.”
